     6	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Sheaf
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Canonical pushforward base change for scheme modules
    10	
    11	For a cartesian square of schemes, `canonicalBaseChangeMap` is the Beck--Chevalley mate
    12	
    13	```text
    14	g^* f_* M --> f'_* (g')^* M.
    15	```
    16	
    17	The two coherence theorems identify its pullback followed by the counit with the pullback of
    18	the original counit.  Invertibility is deliberately not asserted here: it is a property of the
    19	module and square, not part of the construction of the canonical map.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory Limits
    27	
    28	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    29	
    30	/-- The canonical Beck--Chevalley mate for pushforward along a cartesian square. -/
    31	noncomputable def canonicalBaseChangeMap
    32	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    33	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    34	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) :
    35	    Scheme.Modules.pushforward f ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pullback g ⟶
    36	      Scheme.Modules.pullback g' ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pushforward f' :=
    37	  CategoryTheory.mateEquiv
    38	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f)
    39	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f')
    40	    (((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    41	      Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    42	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).hom)
    43	
    44	/-- Pulling back the canonical mate and evaluating recovers its defining pullback telescope. -/
    45	theorem canonicalBaseChangeMap_pullback_counit
    46	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    47	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    48	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (M : X.Modules) :
    49	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback f').map ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app M) ≫
    50	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').counit.app
    51	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj M) =
    52	      ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    53	        Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    54	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).hom).app
    55	          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj M)) ≫
    56	        (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map
    57	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).counit.app M) := by
    58	  rw [canonicalBaseChangeMap]
    59	  exact CategoryTheory.mateEquiv_counit _ _ _ M
    60	
    61	/-- After cancelling the pullback telescope, the base-changed counit is the pulled-back
    62	original counit. -/
    63	theorem canonicalBaseChangeMap_counit_cancel
    64	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    65	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    66	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (M : X.Modules) :
    67	    ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    68	      Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    69	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).inv).app
    70	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj M)) ≫
    71	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f').map ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app M) ≫
    72	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').counit.app
    73	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj M)) =
    74	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map
    75	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).counit.app M) := by
    76	  erw [canonicalBaseChangeMap_pullback_counit]
    77	  erw [Iso.inv_hom_id_app_assoc]
    78	  rfl
    79	
    80	end AlgebraicGeometry

    10	/-!
    11	# THE RIGID ENGINE FIRES FROM A `pic⁰` MEMBERSHIP, WITH NO FIBREWISE BINDER LEFT
    12	
    13	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` fires the RE-4 rigid engine at genus `0` on a
    14	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` under the fibrewise binder
    15	
    16	  `htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1`
    17	
    18	and `Picard/Pic0RingFibrewiseTrivial.lean` proves the corresponding statement for a class in
    19	`pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B)`.  **This file joins the two**: for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
    20	class the binder is discharged, so the engine's conclusions hold with no fibrewise hypothesis
    21	anywhere in the statement.
    22	
    23	## What had to be written, and why it is not a restatement
    24	
    25	Three spelling seams, each of which had to be crossed rather than asserted:
    26	
    27	1. **`relCurveMap` vs the whiskering.**  The engine's base-change naturality
    28	   (`cechPicClass_baseChange`) is stated on `relCurveMap C B B'`, which is *defined* as
    29	   `(C ◁ overSpecMap B B').left` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:160`); the degree
    30	   seam (`Picard/DegreeSeam.lean:81`) is stated on `(C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left`.  The two
    31	   `overSpecMap`s are **independent definitions in different namespaces** — the duplicate pair
    32	   recorded as `I-0144` — and they agree by `rfl` only when `φ` is the canonical algebra map
    33	   `(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k`.  `relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` is
    34	   that identification, and everything downstream needs it.
    35	2. **Field points vs primes.**  `pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps
    36	   into fields; the engine quantifies over `PrimeSpectrum B`.  A residue field *is* such a
    37	   field but the instantiation is a written step, not an observation.
    38	3. **Degree vs triviality.**  What the membership gives at a prime is a vanishing `classDeg`;
    39	   what the engine wants is a trivial class.  The engine's own
    40	   `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts one to the other at genus `0`, and
    41	   it carries **five fibre instance binders** that do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
    42	   `def` barrier; they are installed by hand here, as they are there.
    43	
    44	## What this buys, stated exactly
    45	
    46	The remaining distance from a `pic⁰` class over a test ring to *triviality* of that class is
    47	now: `H¹(C_B, F) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F)` invertible (stalk rank `1` at every prime) **are
    48	available**, unconditionally on the class beyond its being degree-zero and presented.  On the
    49	**divisor/pushforward route** the step that turns an invertible pushforward into a
    50	trivialization of the class is the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`, which my search did not find in
    51	this tree.
    52	
    53	**Scope corrected after review.**  An earlier version of this paragraph called that evaluation
    54	map "the remaining step" for the ring case as such, and asserted its absence from the sibling
    55	project and mathlib as measured.  Both were too strong.  It is the remaining step on *this*
    56	route only: `Picard/Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` reaches the same vanishing through
    57	field-point rigidity, which never produces a divisor and so never needs the evaluation map at
    58	all.  And I verified absence only in AJCR — not in `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, which has
    59	adjunction/counit material, and not in mathlib.
    60	
    61	## What this does NOT do
    62	
    63	* **It does not prove the ring case**, and it is not on the shortest route to it.  The
    64	  evaluation step above is not built here; a fibrewise-trivial class over a ring need not be
    65	  trivial (Traverso–Swan: `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` fails even *given*
    66	  `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)`, measured).  A lane wanting only the vanishing should read
    67	  `Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` first: it reduces the same goal to field-point rigidity
    68	  with no cohomology, no pushforward and no divisor.  What *this* file is for is the
    69	  pushforward route, where `π_*L` invertible is the object of interest in its own right.
    70	* **`IsNoetherianRing B` is inherited**, not introduced: it is the engine's own binder, which
    71	  `Cohomology/DatumDescent.lean:547` is designed to remove.  Nothing here re-proves it and a
    72	  consumer should remove it through that route.
    73	* **The cocycle presentation is a real hypothesis** on the `pic⁰` class, inherited from the
    74	  DAT-4 degree seam.  `exists_cechPicClass_eq` produces a datum for any Čech class on `C_B`,
    75	  but relating *that* datum's class to the plus-class presentation of a `picEt` element is the
    76	  `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam, and it is assumed here rather than proved.
    77	
    78	  **What the binder is, exactly, after measurement — and a first answer CORRECTED.**  The
    79	  *datum* half is free: `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` below produces a presenting datum for
    80	  any class whose affine collapse is `PicEtAff.unit` of *some* relative class (`relPicMk` is
    81	  surjective and `exists_cechPicClass_eq` is total over every `k`-algebra).
    82	
    83	  An earlier version of this paragraph then named ring-level surjectivity of `PicEtAff.unit` as
    84	  the remaining brick, on the ground that `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section`
    85	  (`Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141`) is field-only and section-dependent.  **That was wrong**,
    86	  and a fresh-context audit caught it: `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`
    87	  (`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:161`) supplies the seam at an **arbitrary test ring**, with no field,
    88	  no section and no curve hypothesis, for every class in the range of `relPicToPicEt`.  So the
    89	  seam is not the obstruction it was priced as; `presentation_of_relPicToPicEt` below is that
    90	  observation made usable, and `rigidEngine_of_relPicToPicEt` fires the engine with the
    91	  presentation binder **eliminated** for such classes.
    92	
    93	  What is genuinely missing is therefore **surjectivity of `relPicToPicEt` onto `picEt`** — that
    94	  every étale-plus class over a ring comes from a relative Picard class — which is a different
    95	  statement about a different map, and is what a lane wanting these conclusions at an
    96	  *arbitrary* degree-zero class should target.  `Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199` calls
    97	  membership in that range "honesty" and treats it as a real condition, which is consistent.
    98	* **Genus `0` only.**  At positive genus the fibre classes are not trivial.
    99	
   100	## Main declarations
   101	
   102	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` — the `I-0144` spelling bridge.
   103	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_relPicMk_eq` / `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` — the datum in
   104	  the presentation binder is produced, not assumed, at every test ring.
   105	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.htriv_of_pic0` — **the discharge**: the engine's
   106	  fibrewise binder, from a cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class.
   107	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rigidEngine_of_pic0` — the engine's three
   108	  conclusions with no fibrewise hypothesis.
   109	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` —
   110	  **`π_*L` invertible** from a `pic⁰` membership.
   111	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` — non-vacuity at `ℙ¹` over an
   112	  arbitrary field.
   113	-/

   116	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

   119	
   120	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
   121	
   122	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   123	
   124	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   125	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   126	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]

   131	/-! ## The spelling bridge (`I-0144`) -/
   132	
   133	/-- **The two `overSpecMap`s agree at a residue field.**
   134	
   135	`overSpecMap B κ(p)` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:147`) is built from the
   136	`algebraMap`; `Over.overSpecMap φ` (`Picard/RelPicAlgebra.lean:44`) from an arbitrary
   137	`k`-algebra map.  These are two independent definitions of the same morphism in different
   138	namespaces — the duplicate pair filed as `I-0144` — and at the canonical map
   139	`(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k` they are definitionally equal.
   140	
   141	Stated because the engine's base-change lemmas live on the first spelling and the degree seam
   142	on the second, so no composition of the two is possible without it. -/
   143	theorem relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   144	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
   145	    relCurveMap C B p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   146	      = (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap
   147	          ((Algebra.ofId B p.asIdeal.ResidueField).restrictScalars k)).left :=

     9	# CHART-U(b) — datum-level openness of the chart-membership (witness) locus
    10	(`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6, `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3)
    11	
    12	The affine-level heart of the shared CHART-U(b) brick, stated directly on a pinned
    13	basic-open cocycle datum in the **witness form** the `chartLocus` predicate uses.
    14	
    15	For a datum `D` over an affine base `B`, the locus of primes `q` of `B` at which the
    16	fibre class of `D` at `κ(q)` admits an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`
    17	is Zariski-open in `Spec B`.  This is the single sanctioned openness mechanism of the
    18	campaign (`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing`, Noetherian-free — dat-d §3.5) read
    19	through the two-way datum dictionary of C1
    20	(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness`,
    21	`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-6): the engine open is the complex-form fibre
    22	condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[B] κ(q))`, and the dictionary rewrites it,
    23	pointwise and class-intrinsically, as the effective-witness/h¹-vanishing condition.
    24	
    25	Role in the CHART-U(b) chain (the two unlanded links of §5 risk 1):
    26	
    27	* **the shifted-datum constructor (link 1):** over the étale carrier `B` the plus
    28	  class collapses to an honest Čech class; twisted by the theta layer and DAT-C's
    29	  GAP-1 inverse datum into the `λθᵐ(Σ-shift)⁻¹` class, then extracted
    30	  (`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`) to a datum `D`.  The output of
    31	  that link is exactly a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` — the input of the theorem
    32	  below, whose witness set is then the `chartLocus`-over-`B`.
    33	* **the étale-image openness transport (link 2):** the locus over the test base `A`
    34	  is the image, under the (open, surjective) étale carrier map `Spec B → Spec A`, of
    35	  the open locus this theorem produces — carried to `A` by mathlib's
    36	  `IsOpenMap.isQuotientMap`/`IsQuotientMap.isOpen_preimage` once the fibre-field
    37	  invariance identifies the preimage.
    38	
    39	The theorem is class-intrinsic (any datum in the class has the same witness set, by
    40	(V1a)), so a change of extracted representative is free.
    41	-/

     9	/-!
    10	# THE RIGID ENGINE FIRES AT GENUS `0` ON A FIBREWISE-TRIVIAL CLASS, OVER A TEST RING
    11	
    12	`Picard/Pic0VanishingFieldTest.lean` closed every **field** instance of the degree-zero
    13	Picard vanishing at genus `0`; `Picard/Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean` proved the `∀ T`
    14	binder *is* the `∀` test-ring binder.  What remained was the **ring** case, and the note
    15	released with it priced that as "cohomology and base change, absent from this tree".
    16	
    17	**That price was wrong, and this file is the correction.**  The relevant engine is landed and
    18	is stated over an arbitrary test ring for an arbitrary class:
    19	
    20	* `Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301` — every Čech Picard class on `C_B` is
    21	  `D.cechPicClass` for some `BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π`, at **every** `k`-algebra `B`;
    22	* `Cohomology/GluedSheafEngine.lean:198` — `datumRigidEngine`: from a *fibrewise* `H¹`
    23	  hypothesis, `H¹(C_B, F_D) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F_D)` is finite projective over `B`;
    24	* `Cohomology/GluedSheafDatumFibre.lean:169` — the fibrewise hypothesis follows from a
    25	  witness divisor on the fibre curve with vanishing `H¹`;
    26	* `Picard/DivisorDatumRankOne.lean:148` — on the vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` and
    27	  `χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`, the stalk rank of `H⁰` is `1`.
    28	
    29	What nobody had connected is that at **genus `0`** the fibre inputs of that chain are *free*
    30	rather than expensive, and this file proves exactly that.
    31	
    32	## The two results, and why the hypothesis is the cheap one
    33	
    34	The fibre witness is the **zero divisor**.  Its class is `1` (`picClass_zero`) and its sheaf is
    35	the structure sheaf (`moduleKSheafDivisorSheafZeroIso`), whose `H¹` has `K`-dimension
    36	`genus C` at every field extension `K/k` (`finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus`) — so at genus `0` it
    37	vanishes, at every prime of `B` at once, with no locus, no openness argument and no
    38	spreading-out.  Hence:
    39	
    40	* `subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero` — the engine's `hfib` clause, for **any**
    41	  datum whose fibre classes are trivial;
    42	* `rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero` — `H⁰` of stalk rank `1` at every prime,
    43	  i.e. `π_*L` invertible in the rank spelling, with `χ = 1` supplied by `genus C = 0` rather
    44	  than assumed.
    45	
    46	**The hypothesis is fibre-class triviality, not fibre degree.**  That spelling is deliberate
    47	and is not a strengthening in disguise: at genus `0` the two are *equivalent* by the landed
    48	field-level converse (`eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one`), and
    49	`fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` below is that equivalence at this site.  The
    50	reason to state the theorems on triviality is mechanical, and worth recording because it will
    51	bite the next lane: `classDeg K` carries five instance binders on the fibre curve
    52	(`IsIntegral`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `QuasiCompact`, and both `Module.Finite`
    53	Betti-number clauses) which do not synthesize through the `relCurve` `def` barrier, so a
    54	hypothesis phrased `∀ p, classDeg κ(p) … = 0` **cannot be stated** at a general prime without
    55	`haveI`-installing them first — measured, not guessed.  Triviality of the class needs none of
    56	them.
    57	
    58	## What this does NOT do
    59	
    60	* **It does not discharge the `pic⁰` vanishing at a test ring.**  It supplies the two
    61	  cohomological outputs — `H¹ = 0` and `H⁰` invertible — that the classical proof consumes
    62	  next through the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`.
    63	
    64	  **CORRECTED after a fresh-context audit (`I-1651`).**  An earlier version of this bullet said
    65	  that map "does not exist in this tree, in the sibling project, or in mathlib (measured this
    66	  session)".  **The mathlib half was false and unmeasured**: the map is the counit of
    67	  `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction`
    68	  (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Sheaf.lean`), and the sibling project applies
    69	  `.counit.app` to it in two files.  What is genuinely absent is any theorem saying that counit
    70	  is an **isomorphism** at a sheaf of this kind — that is the real residue, and it is a
    71	  narrower and more defensible claim than the one this bullet used to make.  AJCR's own
    72	  carriers are `Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (ModuleCat R)`, not `Scheme.Modules`, so
    73	  reaching the counit here is itself a port.
    74	* **It says nothing at positive genus**, where the fibre `H¹` is genuinely nonzero and the
    75	  witness above fails at the first step.
    76	* It introduces **no hypothesis on the curve** beyond the three standing binders and
    77	  `genus C = 0`, and no hypothesis on the test ring beyond `IsNoetherianRing` — which
    78	  `Cohomology/DatumDescent.lean:547` is designed to remove and which a consumer should remove
    79	  through that route rather than by re-proving anything here.
    80	
    81	## Main declarations
    82	
    83	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero`
    84	  — **the engine's fibrewise hypothesis, free at genus `0`**.
    85	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rigidEngine_of_genus_zero` — the engine's three
    86	  conclusions with the fibrewise clause discharged.
    87	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero` —
    88	  **`H⁰` of stalk rank `1`**, at every prime.
    89	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` — the
    90	  degree-`0` spelling of the hypothesis implies the triviality spelling, so nothing is lost by
    91	  stating the results on the latter.
    92	-/

   111	/-! ## The fibre inputs at genus `0` -/
   112	
   113	/-- **`H¹` of the structure sheaf of the fibre curve vanishes at genus `0`**, at every field
   114	extension of the base.
   115	
   116	`finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus` computes that dimension as `genus C` on the nose, so this is
   117	the hypothesis read as a dimension count; the `Module.Free` instance the `finrank` criterion
   118	wants is the vector-space one. -/
   119	theorem subsingleton_h1_moduleKSheaf_baseChange_of_genus_zero (hg : genus C = 0)
   120	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
   121	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.moduleKSheaf K) 1) := by
   122	  have h : Module.finrank K
   123	      (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.moduleKSheaf K) 1) = genus C :=
   124	    finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus C K
   125	  rw [hg] at h
   126	  exact (Module.finrank_eq_zero_iff_of_free _ _).mp h
   127	
   128	/-- **The zero divisor is a vanishing witness at genus `0`**: `H¹(𝒪(0)) = H¹(𝒪) = 0`.
   129	
   130	`moduleKSheafDivisorSheafZeroIso` is the identification of the two sheaves; the transport is
   131	`Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv`. -/
   132	theorem subsingleton_h1_divisorSheaf_zero_of_genus_zero (hg : genus C = 0)
   133	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
   134	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.divisorSheaf K
   135	      (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CurveDivisor)) 1) :=
   136	  (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (Scheme.moduleKSheafDivisorSheafZeroIso
   137	    (X := (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left) K) 1).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mp
   138	      (subsingleton_h1_moduleKSheaf_baseChange_of_genus_zero hg K)
   139	
   140	/-- **THE ENGINE'S FIBREWISE HYPOTHESIS, FREE AT GENUS `0`**: for a datum whose fibre class at
   141	the prime `p` is trivial, the complex-form clause `hfib p` of `datumRigidEngine` holds.
   142	
   143	The witness fed to `subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_witness` is the **zero divisor**:
   144	its class is `1` by `picClass_zero`, which is the fibre class by hypothesis, and its `H¹`
   145	vanishes by the lemma above.  No locus, no openness, no spreading-out, and the argument is
   146	uniform in `p`. -/
   147	theorem subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero
   148	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0) (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
   149	    (htriv : (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1) :
   150	    Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
   151	  refine D.subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_witness p ⟨0, ?_, ?_⟩
   152	  · rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, htriv]
   153	    rfl
   154	  · exact subsingleton_h1_divisorSheaf_zero_of_genus_zero hg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   155	
   156	/-! ## The engine, and the rank-`1` export -/
   157	
   158	/-- **The rigid engine at genus `0` on a fibrewise-trivial class**: `H¹(C_B, F_D) = 0` and
   159	`H⁰(C_B, F_D)` finite projective over `B`, with the fibrewise clause discharged by the
   160	genus hypothesis rather than assumed. -/
   161	theorem rigidEngine_of_genus_zero (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) [IsNoetherianRing B]
   162	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
   163	    (htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
   164	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1) :
   165	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 1) ∧
   166	      Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) ∧
   167	      Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) :=
   168	  datumRigidEngine D hπ fun p =>
   169	    D.subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero hg p (htriv p)
   170	
   171	/-- **`H⁰` HAS STALK RANK `1` AT EVERY PRIME** — `π_*L` invertible, in the rank spelling, for a
   172	fibrewise-trivial class on a genus-`0` curve over an arbitrary Noetherian test ring.
   173	
   174	`rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one` is applied at `n := 0`: its χ-normalization
   175	`χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n` is `χ = 1`, which `chi_moduleKSheaf` plus `genus C = 0` supplies, and its
   176	fibre-degree clause is `classDeg κ(p) 1 = 0`, which is `classDeg_one`.  The five fibre
   177	instances are installed by hand — they do not synthesize through the `relCurve` `def`
   178	barrier. -/
   179	theorem rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero
   180	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) [IsNoetherianRing B]
   181	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
   182	    (htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
   183	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1)
   184	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
   185	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   186	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   187	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   188	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   189	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   190	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   191	  haveI : QuasiCompact
   192	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   193	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   194	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
   195	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
   196	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   197	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
   198	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
   199	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   200	  refine D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one (n := 0) hπ ?_
   201	    (fun q => D.subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero hg q (htriv q)) p ?_
   202	  · rw [chi_moduleKSheaf C, hg]
   203	  · rw [htriv p, Nat.cast_zero]
   204	    exact classDeg_one _
   205	
   206	/-! ## The degree spelling is the same hypothesis at genus `0` -/
   207	
   208	/-- **The degree-`0` spelling implies the triviality spelling**, at genus `0`: a fibre class of
   209	degree `0` *is* trivial, by the landed field-level converse
   210	`eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one` at `χ = 1`.
   211	
   212	So the theorems above lose no generality by taking triviality as the hypothesis; what they
   213	gain is that the hypothesis is statable without the five fibre instances `classDeg` needs.
   214	Consumers holding a degree hypothesis at a prime pass through here. -/
   215	theorem fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero
   216	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0) (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
   217	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
   218	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   219	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   220	    [QuasiCompact
   221	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   222	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
   223	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
   224	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
   225	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)]
   226	    (hdeg : classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   227	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 0) :
   228	    (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1 :=
   229	  eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   230	    (chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChange_eq_one_of_genus_zero C p.asIdeal.ResidueField hg) _ hdeg
   231

500	/-! ## Stage (iii): the engine over the descent stage -/
   501	
   502	/-- A finitely generated subalgebra of a commutative algebra over a field is a
   503	Noetherian ring (Hilbert basis through `Algebra.FiniteType`). -/
   504	theorem _root_.Subalgebra.FG.isNoetherianRing {B₀ : Subalgebra k B} (hfg : B₀.FG) :
   505	    IsNoetherianRing (↥B₀) := by
   506	  haveI : Algebra.FiniteType k (↥B₀) := (Subalgebra.fg_iff_finiteType B₀).mp hfg
   507	  exact Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing k (↥B₀)

   509	/-- **RE-5, engine-ready form** (the DAT-B keystone; worksheet §2.3 step 2): a cocycle
   510	datum over an arbitrary commutative `k`-algebra `B` descends to a finitely generated —
   511	hence **Noetherian** — subalgebra stage `B₀ ⊆ B`, with the base-change certificate.
   512	`datumRigidEngine` fires over the stage verbatim; its output transports along `B₀ → B`
   513	through `datumH0BaseChangeEquiv` and the certificate. -/
   514	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_fg_isNoetherianRing_baseChange_eq [IsAffineHom π]
   515	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) :
   516	    ∃ B₀ : Subalgebra k B, B₀.FG ∧ IsNoetherianRing (↥B₀) ∧
   517	      ∃ D₀ : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C (↥B₀) π, D₀.baseChange (B' := B) = D := by
   518	  obtain ⟨B₀, hfg, D₀, hbc⟩ := D.exists_fg_subalgebra_baseChange_eq
   519	  exact ⟨B₀, hfg, hfg.isNoetherianRing, D₀, hbc⟩
   520	
   521	/-- **The classes correspond under `CechPic.map`** (worksheet §3.2, the "consequently"
   522	half): for a descended datum, the class of the given datum on `C_B` is the pullback of
   523	the stage class along the relative-curve comparison — the stage-(1e) naturality
   524	rewritten along the descent certificate. -/
   525	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.descent_cechPicClass [IsAffineHom π]
   526	    {B₀ : Subalgebra k B} {D₀ : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C (↥B₀) π}
   527	    {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π} (hbc : D₀.baseChange (B' := B) = D) :
   528	    D.cechPicClass = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C (↥B₀) B) D₀.cechPicClass := by
   529	  rw [← hbc]
   530	  exact D₀.cechPicClass_baseChange B

   532	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
   533	-- The sheaf-of-modules instances over the subalgebra stage exceed the default
   534	-- synthesis budget (the standing pattern of the engine files).
   535	/-- **The rigid engine over a descent stage** (stage-(iii) wrapper): for a datum over a
   536	finitely generated stage `B₀ ⊆ B` — e.g. one produced by
   537	`exists_fg_isNoetherianRing_baseChange_eq` — the Noetherian hypothesis of
   538	`datumRigidEngine` is automatic: fibrewise vanishing of `H¹` of the stage pair gives
   539	`H¹(C_{B₀}, F) = 0` and `H⁰(C_{B₀}, F)` finite projective over `B₀`.
   540	
   541	Transport to `B`: with `hH1 := (datum_subsingleton_pairH1 D₀ hπ hfib)`, the abstract
   542	ring-map clause `datumH0BaseChangeEquiv D₀ hH1 B` identifies `B ⊗[B₀] H⁰(D₀.sheaf)`

   544	certificate `D₀.baseChange B = D` rewrites every statement about `D` into one about
   545	`D₀.baseChange B`. Threading the kernel onto `H⁰(D.sheaf)` on the nose is DAT-1 stage
   546	(1d-ii) — the recorded seam. -/
   547	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.descentRigidEngine [IsFinite π]
   548	    {B₀ : Subalgebra k B} (hfg : B₀.FG) (D₀ : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C (↥B₀) π)
   549	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

      "body": "DUPLICATION, DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean: the headline \"the FIRST inhabitant of DivFamZar at ANY parameter\" is FALSE over a field, and the uniqueness proof re-derives what two landed quotient-level lemmas already give.\n\nINHABITATION WAS NOT FIRST. exists_divFam_divFamDivisor_eq (DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:143, the landed B-3 hsurj) at D = 0 gives a DivFam C K pi 0 with divFamDivisor = 0, hence DivFamZar C K pi 0 via toZar; divFamFieldEquiv.symm (0, le_rfl, by simp) gives the same class directly, and Quotient.out of it gives a CertifiedDivisorFamily C K pi 0. VERIFIED in a probe importing ONLY DivisorFamilyFieldSurj + DivSchemeAbel, no pic-c file, lake env lean EXIT=0. The correct claim is narrower and still worth having: trivZar is the first inhabitant at a GENERAL TEST RING R, where no field-surjectivity route applies.\n\nUNIQUENESS RE-DERIVES A LANDED LEMMA. presentationDivisor_eq_zero_of_isCertified_zero + divEq_of_isCertified_zero (:103, :114) work per-adaptation and then re-run divEq_of_presentationDivisor_eq. But divFamDivisor_injective (DivisorFamilyFieldEquiv.lean:177) is exactly that step already packaged at the QUOTIENT level, and DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean imports DivisorFamilyFieldEquiv directly. With zero_le_divFamDivisor (DivisorFamilyField.lean:165) and deg_divFamDivisor (DivisorFamilyFieldCRT.lean:376), both also in closure, the whole file's math is:\n  hx : divFamDivisor x = 0 := eq_zero_of_deg_le_zero K (zero_le_divFamDivisor x) (deg rewrite; norm_num)\n  same for y; exact divFamDivisor_injective (hx.trans hy.symm)\nVERIFIED at the file's exact import list minus DivisorFamilyDegreeZero, EXIT=0. Two of the three declarations in the \"Main declarations\" list are avoidable, and the docstring's \"in one line each\" argument describes the longer of two routes without noting the shorter one exists.\n\nALSO: instSubsingletonDivFamZarZero and uniqueZeroOfField carry [LocallyOfFiniteType (relCurve C K over Spec K)] which is NOT load-bearing: it is inferInstance from the SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 binder two lines up (Smooth => LocallyOfFiniteType). Verified by re-elaborating both without it, EXIT=0.",

      "body": "REPLACING A HAND-ROLLED HYPOTHESIS BY 'THE STANDARD ONE' CAN STRENGTHEN IT INTO FALSITY -- and the test is a REFUTATION probe at the intended object, not a satisfiability witness.\n\nMEASURED (pic-e, AJC 0095 r7). I built the vocabulary the project was missing (graded prime avoidance => FiniteInAffine for projective schemes, all sorry-free), then restated the seam's antecedent with IsProjective of the representing scheme in place of the elementary FiniteInAffine, and committed 'entirely in standard vocabulary, no condition invented in this project'. I ran THREE vacuity checks and all three PASSED: the new conjunct is satisfiable (Spec k is projective over itself), it is NOT free (exact? fails at an arbitrary object), and the new antecedent does not close hypothesis-free. A fresh-context audit then refuted it in one step.\n\nWHY THE CHECKS MISSED IT. Every one of them asks 'could this hypothesis hold SOMEWHERE?'. None asks 'does it hold AT THE OBJECT THE STATEMENT IS ABOUT?'. IsProjective over a field forces IsProper, hence UniversallyClosed, hence CompactSpace over the compact Spec k -- and Pic_{C/k} is a disjoint union over deg in Z, so it is not quasi-compact. The antecedent is FALSE at its only intended witness. Satisfiability elsewhere is exactly what makes that invisible.\n\nWORSE: my own project already had the refutation. Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean exists to record this as 'trap (c): a P -> Q whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting', with the general theorems to check it -- and I had imported nothing from it. The strengthening was FROM a weak condition my own file proved holds at the curve TO one my own project proved fails at the Picard scheme.\n\nTHE GENERALISABLE RULE. When you replace a hypothesis H by a 'more standard' H', H' => H is not enough -- that direction is what makes the substitution LOOK conservative. Ask what H' implies that H does not (here: quasi-compactness), then check that consequence at the intended witness. And grep your own tree for a file whose title is a negation ('NotProper', 'NoGo', 'Refute') before publishing a strengthening: the counterexample is often already landed one import away.\n\nALSO: the weakened repair is where tautologies hide. My first repair -- 'every finite set that lies in a good open lies in an affine open' -- is PROVABLE for every scheme with its hypothesis unused. Elaborate the candidate weakening with the binder discarded before shipping it (pic-g filed the same shape as I-1660 the same day).",

      "body": "AN 'ONLY PRODUCER IS FIELD-ONLY' CLAIM IS A CENSUS OF THE NAME YOU GUESSED, AND THE RING-LEVEL VERSION IS OFTEN LANDED UNDER A DIFFERENT MAP.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g 0096 r6, refuted by a fresh-context audit of my own file). I published that the picEtAffineEquiv/unit presentation seam has exactly one general producer -- PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section -- that it is stated over a FIELD and needs a curve section there, and that ring-level surjectivity of PicEtAff.unit is therefore the honest next brick. Every clause was checkable and the conclusion was false: picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:161) supplies the same seam at an ARBITRARY test RING, no field, no section, no curve binder, with 11 call sites.\n\nWHY MY CENSUS MISSED IT, and this is the reusable part. I searched for producers of the SEAM'S NAME -- surjectivity of  -- because that is the shape of the conclusion I wanted. The landed producer is not about 's surjectivity at all: it is an AFFINE-CONSISTENCY lemma for a DIFFERENT map (relPicToPicEt) which happens to have the seam as its conclusion. A grep for 'unit_surjective' finds it never; a search for the CONCLUSION 'picEtAffineEquiv _ = PicEtAff.unit _ _' finds it first.\n\nSO THE RULE: when you are about to write 'the only producer is X, and X is too strong', search for the CONCLUSION you need, not for the strengthened statement whose name you have. The name census answers 'who proved this lemma'; the obligation is 'who lands this Prop', and a lemma about another map can land it while carrying none of the binders you were about to price.\n\nAND THE SECOND-ORDER COST, which is why this is worth a memory item rather than a header note: the false claim RELOCATED THE GAP.       "body": "A \"TRAP, MEASURED -- DO NOT ROUTE VIA X\" NOTE IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FALSE CLAIM A LANE CAN SHIP, AND THE CHEAPEST TEST IS TO GREP WHETHER A SIBLING FILE ALREADY DOES X.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (AJCR, pic-c 0092 r5, Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean:33-38). A lane recorded, in a file header, a commit message, and a direct message to another lane: \"going through chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle C K produces the same object under a different Over instance, and the two chi terms DO NOT UNIFY -- measured\". It reads like exactly the kind of hard-won spelling fact worth broadcasting, and the receiving lane accepted it.\n\nIt is false. The bundled route closes with one `change` to the bundled spelling followed by `simpa`, at DEFAULT heartbeats. What had been measured was that one `simpa` failed without the `change`, i.e. a fact about a tactic invocation, published as a fact about two objects.\n\nTHE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT COST ONE GREP. A sibling lane had written the prohibited proof, at a concrete curve, in the same hour, and it was at HEAD and root-imported: Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean:83-99 uses chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle with the same change + simpa. So before publishing \"route X does not work\", grep the tree for X: a live use site refutes the prohibition outright, and its presence in a file you did not write is more likely than it feels, because a prohibition is usually discovered exactly when two lanes are on the same object.\n\nWHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY OVERCLAIM. A positive overclaim gets tested when someone tries to use the result. A prohibition is never tested -- its whole function is to stop people trying -- so it can survive indefinitely and it forecloses a cheap route for every later round. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[exculpatory-sentence-is-a-claim]], but with a longer half-life.\n\nCOROLLARY, same round, same file: unexplained `set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000` raises with a comment asserting the default is exceeded. Copying both files verbatim with the default budget: EXIT=0, all six declarations. A budget raise is a claim too, and re-running the file at the default is a 40-second check.",

      "body": "A LOCALISATION REDUCTION IS EMPTIED BY THE CONSUMER OWN OUTER QUANTIFIER, AND EVERY PER-STATEMENT CHECK PASSES.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g, AJCR 0096 r7, Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean; audit I-1657/I-1660, reproduced by me).\n\nWHAT HAPPENED. I reduced an obligation P(A) at an arbitrary test algebra to a pointwise-local form: for every prime p of A, some f outside p with P(Localization.Away f). At a FIXED A that is a real reduction with no route back, and I verified it. I then composed it over all A into two producers of the goal object -- and those hypotheses are LOGICALLY EQUIVALENT to the global ones they were meant to weaken, because Localization.Away f is ITSELF a test algebra, so the consumer own forall-A already ranges over it. The converse is one line with the trivial witness f = 1.\n\nWHY EVERY CHECK PASSED. Sorry-free, axiom-clean against a sorryAx control, rooted, build green, non-vacuous (both hypotheses used, linter clean), and the fixed-A lemma genuinely is a reduction. Nothing local to any statement is wrong. The defect is the INTERACTION between my inner quantifier and the consumer outer one, and no per-statement check can see it.\n\nTHE TEST, and it costs one probe: before pricing a localisation, pointwise, or restriction reduction as progress, PROVE THE CONVERSE WITH THE TRIVIAL WITNESS -- f = 1, the identity localisation, V = top, the whole space. If it closes, the reduction only helps at a FIXED base object, and you must then check whether the consumer has that shape. Mine did not.\n\nSECOND, SMALLER TRAP FROM THE SAME FILE: my \"local ring\" interface was about Localization.Away f, which is a BASIC OPEN and not a local ring (IsLocalRing fails to synthesize). A lane with a genuinely local computation holds Localization.AtPrime, and the AtPrime-to-Away bridge is spreading out -- ask which one your consumer actually has before naming the interface.\n\nSibling of \"substitute the trivial value in layer one\" and \"free factor vs localisation\".",

      "body": "A --summary WRITE IS A SILENT DESTRUCTIVE EDIT, AND THE TOOL'S OWN OUTPUT CANNOT SHOW IT. Check the commit STAT, not the command's success line.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, AJCR 0092 r1). I claimed a row with roadmap set --owner --status --summary. The CLI printed 'Updated roadmap item' and nothing else. The commit stat then read 46 insertions / 117 DELETIONS. --summary REPLACES; the 117 lines were review-ajcr's rank-elevation analysis of that exact fork, TWO author self-retractions inside it, and the row's stated live target. I had read the row earlier in the session, but through roadmap list, which truncates -- so I never saw the body I was about to overwrite.\n\nWHY THE EXISTING LESSONS DO NOT COVER IT. The workspace has roadmap-yaml-edit-reverts-owner (a prose edit writing a stale OWNER over a live claim) and several items about staged deletions of other lanes' FILES. This is neither: the owner field was fine, no file was staged D, the write was to a row I legitimately hold, and the loss was entirely inside one YAML string. Every file-level check passes.\n\nTHE RULE, cheap and it is the only one that works. After any roadmap set --summary, read the commit stat. A deletion count above a handful means you replaced prose you never read. Recover with git show <commit>^:<path>, merge the prior summary verbatim, append yours behind a marker saying what happened, and re-verify a distinctive phrase from the old text is present.\n\nTHE SHARPER POINT. The destroyed text contained a retraction whose lesson was 'a probe with the hypothesis as a BINDER measures the conversion, so the control looks audited' -- i.e. I deleted a warning about exactly the class of error a reviewer had just caught me making elsewhere in the same session. Board prose is where a lane's corrections live, and it is the least protected thing in the workspace: no build breaks, no test fails, no file appears deleted.",

      "body": "A THREE-LANE COMPOSITION IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY PER-ROW CHECK, AND THE ROWS WILL EACH TELL YOU THE WORK IS ELSEWHERE.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-e, AJC, 0095 r6). Three sorry-free theorems from three different lanes composed into a verbatim derivation of the project's central sorry from the classical pointed theorem: the unconditional finite-GALOIS-level rational point (Curve/), the picSharp->picEt transport (PicEtSubcanonical), and the lftFree descent step with hq and hcov already internal (PicEtGaloisQuotient). Eleven declarations, all axiom-clean, three commits.\n\nNO ROW MENTIONED THE OTHER TWO. The descent-assembly row listed FOUR open inputs; three were already discharged elsewhere. The seam docstring's own 'what remains' sentence listed three items, one of which was closed and one of which was DONE-AND-CALLED-REMAINING. Every row was individually plausible and internally consistent; the composition existed only across them.\n\nTHE MECHANISM, and why the usual checks miss it: each row is maintained by the lane that owns it, and a lane records what IT owes, not what another lane has since supplied. So a row goes stale in the CHEAP direction -- it schedules work that exists -- and nothing re-reads it, because a list of remaining obligations reads as self-criticism. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[unavoidable-is-not-geometric]], but distributed: no single sentence is wrong enough to notice.\n\nTHE CHECK THAT FINDS IT, and it is cheap: take the consumer theorem's LITERAL binder list -- #check the one a costing tells you to aim at -- and ask of EACH binder, separately, 'does a producer for exactly this exist at HEAD?'. Not 'is this gap open' (the row answers that) but 'is this BINDER discharged'. At the spelling that matters, seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree, three of four were gone and the fourth was an instance binder no row named. A four-item gap list and a one-item binder list were both accurate about different things.\n\nCOROLLARY, the part that cost me a withdrawal: after composing, price the RESULT against the WEAKEST antecedent your proof consumes, not the shape the hand-off wants. My first antecedent carried IsSeparated, which is provably free from the conclusion's own representation, and a reduction whose antecedent contains a free conjunct misreports exactly the number it exists to report. Related: [[price-the-consumer-carrier]], [[audit-the-goals-antecedents-not-the-lemmas]].",

      "body": "VANISHING-VOCABULARY SPELLINGS ARE ONE ANTECEDENT -- and the commit that ships the 'reduced' producer often ships the iff that proves it is a re-spelling.\n\nAJC DivFamilyZero.lean, AJC.picrep.divzero, pic-e runs 0095->0105. Over three rounds the same lane landed three producers of Div0-representable, each 'reducing' the obligation to a fresh vocabulary:\n  _of_isZero               : IsZero x.F\n  _of_forall_subsingleton_sections : forall V, Subsingleton Gamma(x.F,V)\n  _of_forall_isEmpty_schematicSupport : IsEmpty(schematicSupport x.F)\nEach docstring bills its antecedent as 'the sharpest/purest/most-geometric honest form.' At every DivFamily x.F is quasicoherent, and the file itself ships isZero_iff_forall_subsingleton_sections and isZero_iff_isEmpty_schematicSupport -- so the three antecedents are PROVABLY EQUIVALENT (all = IsZero x.F). None is weaker. The obligation HasFiberDeg 0 -> IsZero x.F is untouched; only the vocabulary on its RHS rotates.\n\nTHE TELL, sharper than I-1622: when a 'reduction' commit also lands an IFF between the new antecedent and the old one, the iff IS the proof that no reduction happened. Emptiness-of-support, subsingleton-sections, and IsZero are one node with three names; a producer parameterised on any of them is the same producer. Before crediting 'reduced to X', rw the shipped iffs and check whether the new antecedent closes the old goal with no hypotheses -- if it does, it is coordinates, not distance. The real distance for divzero lives in DivSupportQuasiFinite.lean (carrier bridge + degree-0=>empty-fibre), which no spelling of the RHS moves.",

      "body": "DivQProjBundle is not Kleiman quasi-projectivity\n\nMeasured: DivSchemeQProj.lean:214-245 labels DivQProjBundle quasi-projective as consumed, but its fields are only a closed immersion into the Grassmannian pair, finite affine atlas, qc, lft, and separatedness; its own boundary says Plucker projectivity is absent.
